intro: Word for medical billers on Mac is the desktop Word app, and it handles most of the paperwork a billing office produces. That means appeal letters, patient letters and payer forms, usually built from templates and mail merges from Excel. This page covers the Word work billers repeat most, the Mac settings that trip people up, and where Lazur helps while you type.
tldr: Build appeal and patient letters from a DOCX template with bracketed tags for each changing detail.
Run mail merges from one Excel sheet, in the Word desktop app, from the Mailings tab.
Check your build and test a save first. Microsoft flagged a July 13, 2026 edit issue for some Office apps on macOS.
Lazur points at menus, guides you one click at a time and dictates text. It does not click for you.

blocks.text: This page covers the Word work that medical billers do most on a Mac. That includes appeal letters, patient letters, mail merges from Excel, and the review steps before anything goes to a payer. It also shows where voice help from Lazur fits, and where it does not.
What medical billers do in Word on Mac

Most billing work in Word is repetitive. You open a letter you have sent before. You swap in a claim number, a date of service and a denial reason. Then you save it under a new name and send it. The skills that matter are plain ones: templates, merge fields, find and replace, and a clean PDF for the payer.

Here is a simple example. An appeal for a denied claim usually has the same parts every time. There is a header with your practice details, a short opening, the claim facts, the reason you disagree, an attachments list and a closing. Only the middle changes. Build that letter once as a template, and the next one takes minutes.
The biggest time sink is rarely typing. It is hunting for the right version, the right fields and the right wording. A template with clear placeholders fixes most of that problem.
Why appeal letters take so much time

Survey data gives a rough picture of the workload. Weave's 2026 State of Healthcare Pulse Survey covered 285 respondents. They included practice owners, office managers and front desk staff. Of them, 63% spend an hour or more a day on manual data entry, and 32% spend two hours or more.
That survey does not measure Word use. It also does not say when the fieldwork happened. Treat it as a sign of the workload, not as a benchmark for your office.

The denial numbers explain why appeals matter. KFF reports that Medicare Advantage insurers decided 52.8 million prior authorization requests in 2024. Insurers denied 4.1 million of them, or 7.7%, in full or in part.

Most denials never get appealed. Only 11.5% of denied requests were appealed. Of the appeals that were filed, 80.7% were partly or fully overturned. Those figures cover prior authorization, not claims payment, and KFF excludes withdrawn or dismissed requests.
Read those numbers as a reason to build a good letter, not a reason to appeal everything. A letter you can produce in minutes makes the appeals you choose to send easier to file on time.
Check your Word version and license first

Start with the build number. The latest Word for Mac release listed by Microsoft is version 16.114.4, build 26110224, dated November 4, 2026. The two builds before it are 16.114.3 from October 27, 2026 and 16.114.2 from October 26, 2026.

To check yours, open Word > About Microsoft Word. To update, open Help > Check for Updates. A current build gives you Microsoft's latest fixes, so it is the safe place to start before you build templates.

blocks.title: Possible edit lock from July 13, 2026
blocks.text: Microsoft's known issues page says that starting July 13, 2026, some Office apps on macOS may open and print files but not edit, save or create them. It names Microsoft 365 subscribers and non-subscription Office 2019 and 2021 users. That date has passed, and the page does not confirm enforcement. Test before you rely on a file.
Run a short test before you start. Each check below takes a minute or two. If any check fails, stop and ask your IT contact or your Microsoft 365 admin about your license before you send anything.

items: Word > About Microsoft Word shows your build number.
Help > Check for Updates installs the latest release.
A new blank document must save to your Desktop.
An existing letter must save after one small edit.
Print a test page from the desktop app, not Word for the web.

blocks.text: Templates for appeals and patient letters

You do not have to write every template from scratch. Free starting points exist, and they come in two formats: DOCX for editing and PDF for reading. On a Mac, DOCX is the format you want. A PDF needs a conversion step before you can fill it in.

The National Marrow Donor Program publishes a standard Medicare appeal letter template in DOCX for each of the five levels of the standard Medicare appeals process. The page links to terms of use and shows a copyright notice. It does not state specific license terms, so read the terms before you reuse the file in your practice.

Wonder.legal offers a free, one-page medical claim letter in Word and PDF. You generate it from an online form. The site warns that an insurer may require particular information for a claim to be processed. It advises you to check the insurer's website or helpline first.

items: Check the insurer's own requirements for the claim type.
Confirm the license or terms of use for the file.
Delete sample names, addresses and old comments from the document.
Save a copy as your master file. Never edit the original.

blocks.text: Build a reusable appeal template with placeholders

A template works when the changing parts are easy to spot. Put a plain tag such as [CLAIM_NUMBER] or [PATIENT_NAME] in each spot that changes. Then search for the tags before you send anything. Any tag left in the letter shows you what you missed.

items: Open the template in Word for Mac and save a copy under a new name.
Replace each changing detail with a bracketed tag, one tag per field.
Open Find and Replace with ⌥⌘F and search for an opening bracket.
Fix every hit, then search for the closing bracket too.
Choose File > Save As, then pick Word Template (.dotx) as the format.
Open the .dotx file each time you need a letter, so Word makes a new untitled copy.

blocks.text: Watch for one edge case. If a tag looks right but Find misses it, the text probably has different formatting inside it. Retype the tag in one go, then search again.

The most common template mistake is a master that still holds the last patient's facts. Clear the body before you save the master. If you can, lock the file in Finder with Get Info > Locked so nobody edits it by accident.
Mail merge from Excel on Mac, step by step

Mail merge is where Word saves the most time. It takes one letter and fills it with a row of data for each recipient. Microsoft says Excel works well as a data source when all the data sits on one sheet and is formatted so Word can read it.

Two limits matter here. Mail merge runs in the Word desktop app. Word for the web lets you keep existing mail merge settings, but you cannot run a merge or change those settings. Split large workbooks into one sheet before you start.

items: In Excel, put field names in row 1, one per column, such as Patient, Claim, Date of Service and Payer.
Remove merged cells and blank columns between fields.
Format ZIP codes and claim numbers as Text, so leading zeros survive.
Save the workbook and close it before you start the merge.
In Word, open your letter template and choose Mailings > Start Mail Merge > Letters.
Choose Mailings > Select Recipients > Use an Existing List, then pick the workbook and its sheet.
Click where a name goes, then choose Mailings > Insert Merge Field and pick the column.
Choose Mailings > Preview Results and use the arrows to check each record.
Choose Mailings > Finish & Merge > Edit Individual Documents to get one file with every letter.

blocks.text: Menu names can change between versions. A Microsoft Q&A thread about Word for Mac 2024 describes Mailings as a Ribbon tab, with Start Mail Merge, Labels and Select Recipients in it. A commenter in that thread says a Tools menu listing appears in Word 2024 only. If your menus differ, look for the Mailings tab on the Ribbon first.
Mistakes that break a mail merge on Mac

items: Running the merge in Word for the web. The merge options are missing or greyed out there.
Keeping data across several sheets. Word reads one sheet, so the other rows never appear.
Losing ZIP code zeros. A code like 02134 becomes 2134 when Excel stores it as a number.
Blank fields leaving empty lines. Check Preview Results for every letter with an optional line.
Sending the merged file without a read-through. Scan the first, a middle and the last letter at minimum.

blocks.text: The last mistake costs the most. A merge can be perfect in its mechanics and still send the wrong claim number to the wrong payer. Compare a few letters against the tracker before you export anything.
Labels and envelopes for statements and mailings

Mail merge also makes labels and envelopes. The steps start the same way. Choose Mailings > Start Mail Merge > Labels, pick your label product, then use Mailings > Select Recipients to link the Excel list. Insert the merge fields into the label layout and preview before you print.
Test on plain paper first. Hold a printed sheet up to a sheet of labels to check alignment. A misaligned run wastes a whole sheet of labels, so the test is worth the minute it takes.
Track Changes and Compare for payer letter reviews

Review matters when more than one person touches a letter. Track Changes records each edit so a supervisor can accept or reject it. On a Mac, turn it on with ⌘⇧E or from the Review tab. Add a comment with ⌥⌘A when a change needs an explanation.

Compare sets two versions side by side. Use Review > Compare to see what changed between your draft and the version you sent last month. Microsoft's known issues page lists a problem where files appear greyed out in the Compare feature. If that happens, check the page for the current workaround before you assume the file is broken.
Save, export and print without losing your work

Saving is where many billers lose time. Microsoft lists a known issue where saving a document as PDF to an online location changes it to a .docx file. Save the document to your Mac first, then export the PDF from that local copy. Use File > Export and choose PDF.

Two more known issues matter for this work. Word can prompt you to save locally after a stretch of idle time with no edits, and Microsoft says it is investigating that prompt. Printing from Word for the web may also fail on macOS. Print from the desktop app instead.

rows: Use the desktop app, not Word for the web
Mailings > Select Recipients > Use an Existing List
One sheet only, saved and closed
Look for empty lines and lost ZIP zeros
Accept or reject changes before sending
Greyed-out files are a known issue
Save locally first, not to an online location

blocks.text: Where Lazur helps while you work in Word

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. It lives in the notch. Hold ⌥⌘, Option and Command together, to ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud. That helps when a menu is buried and you do not want to hunt through every tab.

Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it on your screen. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click before it moves on. You stay in control of Word the whole time.

Dictation works in any app. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor. Lazur also keeps snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots. Those help with the payer terms and names that your spell checker keeps flagging.

Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for Word. Think of it as a guide that sits beside Word. For the wider Word picture, see the [Word for Mac page](/apps/word).
Questions billers ask Lazur in Word

The most useful questions are specific. Ask about the menu you can see, the sentence you are writing, or the error on screen. A question like where is the merge button gets a better answer than help me with billing.

Lazur can also help you read a denial letter on screen. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask what the payer is asking for. Then check that answer against the letter yourself. A voice answer is a starting point, not the payer's rule.

Dictation suits the parts you would otherwise type from memory. Draft the opening of an appeal by voice, then fix the details by hand. Numbers are easy to mishear, so check every claim number by eye before it goes out.
Patient data, privacy and HIPAA questions

Medical billing puts patient data on screen all day. Before you use voice help near that data, read the product facts. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

Those are product statements, not a compliance review. This page does not say that Lazur is HIPAA compliant. Ask your compliance lead before you put patient names, dates of birth or member IDs in front of any AI tool.

blocks.title: Share less while you ask
blocks.text: Close unrelated patient files before you hold the shortcut. Use the claim number instead of the full name when the letter allows it. Redact the screen when you can, then ask your question out loud.
A repeatable workflow for denied claims
Build the workflow once. Then each denial follows the same path. This sequence works for many billing offices. Adapt it to your practice rules and your payer's requirements.

items: Save the payer letter to a claims folder, named with the claim number and the date.
Pick the template for that denial type. Keep one master per type.
Run the mail merge from your [Excel claim tracker](/for/medical-billers/excel), or fill in the template by hand for one-off cases.
Use Find with ⌥⌘F to catch any leftover bracket tags.
Turn on Track Changes if a supervisor needs to review the draft.
Export the final letter as PDF from a local copy, then attach the payer's required documents.
Send the packet, then log the send date in your tracker so the next follow-up is never a guess.

blocks.text: Each step is small. Together they keep a stack of denials from becoming a backlog. If your team also sends payer emails, the [Outlook guide for medical billers](/for/medical-billers/outlook) covers templates and rules for that side of the work.
Common mistakes outside mail merge
Templates from strangers can carry old data. Open them in a test copy and search for names, dates and claim numbers you do not recognize. Save your master only after that check passes.

Some guides for older Word versions list menus that no longer match your window. Use the Ribbon tab names in the window in front of you. If you hold ⌥⌘ and ask Lazur where the command is, it can point at the right tab.
What to do this week

items: Check your build number with Word > About Microsoft Word.
Run the save test on a blank document and on a copy of a real letter.
Build one appeal template with bracketed tags and save it as a .dotx file.
Run a small test merge with fake data before you touch live claims.
Read the Microsoft known issues page for Compare and PDF saving.
Look at [pricing](/pricing) only after you know the workflow fits your day.

faq.question: Does Word for Mac have mail merge for billing letters?
faq.answer: Yes. Word for Mac runs mail merge from the Mailings tab in the desktop app. Use an Excel sheet with one row per recipient. Word for the web keeps existing merge settings, but it cannot run a merge or change them, so do the merge in the desktop app.

faq.question: Can I use Word for the web for appeal letters?
faq.answer: You can open and edit documents there, but do not rely on it for mail merge. Microsoft's known issues page also says printing from Word for the web may fail on macOS. Print from the desktop app instead.

faq.question: Will Word on Mac stop editing files after July 13, 2026?
faq.answer: Microsoft's known issues page says that starting July 13, 2026, some Office apps on macOS may open and print files but not edit, save or create them. The page does not confirm whether that applies to every license. Test a new document and a save before you rely on it, and ask your IT contact if a save fails.

faq.question: Where do I get a Medicare appeal letter template?
faq.answer: The National Marrow Donor Program offers a standard Medicare appeal letter template in DOCX for each of the five levels of the standard Medicare appeals process. Read the terms of use on that page before you reuse the file. Wonder.legal also offers a free one-page medical claim letter in Word and PDF.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons or edit my Word files?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at things, guides you one click at a time, answers out loud, and dictates or drafts text. It does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It is not an add-in for Word.

faq.question: Is Lazur HIPAA compliant?
faq.answer: This page does not say so. The product facts cover what Lazur listens to, when it looks at the screen, and what goes to AI providers to answer. Talk to your compliance lead before you use voice help near patient data.

faq.question: Why does a merged ZIP code lose its leading zero?
faq.answer: Excel stores a ZIP code like 02134 as the number 2134 unless the cell is formatted as Text. Format the column as Text before you save the workbook, then run the merge again. Check the first few letters to confirm.

faq.question: Which Word version should a billing office use?
faq.answer: Use the current release. Microsoft's update history lists version 16.114.4, build 26110224, dated November 4, 2026, as the latest Word for Mac release. Check Word > About Microsoft Word, then run Help > Check for Updates.
